actions.register.title: hc.actions.register(namespace, handlers)
actions.register.signature: (namespace: string, handlers: Record<string, () => void | Promise<void>>) => Disposable
actions.register.description:
**Manifest:** none. Requires the `ui` permission.

Registers plugin actions in HarborClient's Action menu. Users open the Action menu, type `#`, and see actions grouped as `Namespace: Label`.

Use this for lightweight commands that should be discoverable without adding a persistent menu item or toolbar button. Because actions are dynamic, they do not need `manifest.contributes.commands` entries, but the plugin must include the `ui` permission.

With that plugin installed, typing `#curl` in the Action menu shows:

- `cURL: View`
- `cURL: Close`

params.name: namespace
params.description: Prefix shown before each action label

params.name: handlers
params.description: Action labels mapped to handlers run on selection

ai.copyToChat.title: hc.ai.copyToChat(input)
ai.copyToChat.description:
Opens the AI sidebar, ensures a chat exists, stores a snapshot, and queues the badge token in the composer.

Default grammar — pass `key` (host builds `@plugin…`):

Custom match — pass the full `token` including `@`:

Context longer than 100,000 characters is truncated with a clear marker. Pair with [`CopyToChatButton`](/components/copy-to-chat-button) (or a CodeEditor `copy-to-chat` toolbar action) and call `hc.ai.copyToChat` from `onSelect`.

See [Chat pointers](/examples/chat-pointers) for a full walkthrough.

ai.instructions.add.title: hc.ai.instructions.add(text)
ai.instructions.add.description:
Appends a static fragment to the agent system prompt while the returned disposable is active. Whitespace-only strings are ignored. `hc.ai.instructions.list` returns this plugin's currently registered fragments.

Merge order for the default agent path: Harbor base prompt → chat-pointer `agentGuidance` → static `instructions.add` fragments → (per turn) ephemeral system message from `onBeforeTurn` → `ctx.instructions.push`.

ai.onAfterTurn.title: hc.ai.onAfterTurn(handler)
ai.onAfterTurn.description: Runs once when the turn finishes (completed, cancelled, or error). The context is read-only: `userMessage`, `assistantMessage`, `status`, optional `error`, and `stats` (`stepCount`, `toolCallCount`, `durationMs`).

ai.onBeforeTurn.title: hc.ai.onBeforeTurn(handler)
ai.onBeforeTurn.description: Runs once when the user sends a chat message, **before** the first LLM completion step. The handler receives a mutable context:

ai.registerChatPointer.title: hc.ai.registerChatPointer(config)
ai.registerChatPointer.description:
**Default grammar** (`match` / `parse` omitted) — tokens are `@plugin.<pluginId>.<id>.<key>` with an optional `#start.end` selection suffix:

**Custom grammar** — supply both `match` (body after `@`, as a `RegExp` or source string) and `parse`. Patterns that can match reserved builtin shapes (`plugin`, `request`, `res`, `term`, …) are rejected:

`id` must match `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`. `parse` returns `{ key, selection? }` or `null`; the host fills `kind: 'plugin'`, `pluginId`, and token offsets. Composer highlighting uses a sync host fallback; your `parse` is authoritative at copy and send/validate over IPC.

commands.execute.title: hc.commands.execute(id, ...args)
commands.execute.description: Runs a registered command programmatically — for example to open a main view from another part of your plugin.

commands.register.title: hc.commands.register(id, handler)
commands.register.signature: (id: string, handler: (...args: unknown[]) => void | Promise<void>) => Disposable
commands.register.description:
**Manifest:** matching `contributes.commands` entry

Registers a command handler. The `id` must match a command declared in the manifest and referenced by menu, toolbar, or context menu contributions.

database.all.title: hc.database.all(sql, params?)
database.all.signature: <T = Record<string, unknown>>(sql: string, params?: unknown[]) => Promise<T[]>

database.exec.title: hc.database.exec(sql)
database.exec.description: Executes a multi-statement SQL script (typically migrations). Rejects scripts containing `ATTACH`, `DETACH`, or `load_extension`.

database.get.title: hc.database.get(sql, params?)
database.get.signature: <T = Record<string, unknown>>(sql: string, params?: unknown[]) => Promise<T | undefined>
database.get.description: Returns the first row, or `undefined` when no row matches.

database.run.title: hc.database.run(sql, params?)
database.run.description: Runs an `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE` statement. Returns `{ changes, lastInsertRowid }`.

database.transaction.title: hc.database.transaction(fn)
database.transaction.description:
Runs `fn` inside an exclusive transaction. The `tx` object exposes `get`, `all`, and `run` bound to the same transaction.

Plugin database files are included in HarborClient `.hcb` backups and removed when the plugin is uninstalled.

fs.pickDirectory.title: hc.fs.pickDirectory(defaultPath?)
fs.pickDirectory.description: Opens a native directory picker. Returns the selected directory path, or `null` when canceled. Requires the `filesystem:pick` permission.

fs.pickFile.title: hc.fs.pickFile(options?)
fs.pickFile.description: Opens a native file picker. Returns absolute paths for the selected files, or an empty array when the dialog is canceled. Requires the `filesystem:pick` permission.

fs.readFile.title: hc.fs.readFile(path)
fs.readFile.description: Reads a UTF-8 text file from an allowlisted path. Requires the `filesystem:read` permission.

fs.saveFile.title: hc.fs.saveFile(content, options?)
fs.saveFile.description: Opens a native save dialog and writes `content` to the chosen path. Returns the saved path, or `null` when canceled. Requires the `filesystem:pick` and `filesystem:write` permissions.

fs.writeBytes.title: hc.fs.writeBytes(path, bytes)
fs.writeBytes.description: Writes binary bytes to an allowlisted path. Relative paths resolve under the plugin package directory. Returns the absolute path written. Requires the `filesystem:write` permission.

fs.writeFile.title: hc.fs.writeFile(path, content)
fs.writeFile.description: Writes UTF-8 text to an allowlisted path. Requires the `filesystem:write` permission.

host.applyRequestDraft.title: hc.host.applyRequestDraft(payload)
host.applyRequestDraft.description:
Updates the active request editor tab in place. Provided fields replace the
corresponding draft values; when `headers` or `params` are supplied, those
tables are replaced entirely. The tab becomes dirty, so the user still decides
whether to save the changed request to its collection.

`applyRequestDraft` throws when there is no active request tab or when a field is
invalid. Show parse/update failures inline in your plugin UI when the user needs
to fix input.

host.createCollection.title: hc.host.createCollection(payload)
host.createCollection.description: Bulk-creates a collection with folders and saved requests. Requests sharing the same `folder` string are grouped into one folder; requests without `folder` are created at the collection root.

host.fetch.title: hc.host.fetch(input, init?)
host.fetch.signature: (input: string | URL | { url: string }, init?: PluginFetchInit) => Promise<PluginFetchResponse>
host.fetch.description: Sends one outbound HTTP request through the main-process pipeline using the native `fetch(input, init?)` signature. Requires the `network` permission.

host.loadRequest.title: hc.host.loadRequest(requestId)
host.loadRequest.description: Opens a saved collection request or focuses an existing tab for it.

examples.code: await hc.host.loadRequest(42);

host.openImageView.title: hc.host.openImageView(payload)
host.openImageView.description:
Opens or focuses an image-view page tab. Use this to display screenshots, logos,
generated charts, or import previews in a dedicated tab with **Copy location**
and **Download** actions. Prefer this typed API over
`hc.commands.execute('harborclient:openImageView', payload)`.

See also [Renderer API → hc.host](/api/host).

**Payload rules**

- Provide exactly one source: `path`, `url`, `dataUrl`, or `base64` with
  `contentType`.
- `fileName` is optional for `path` and `url` (derived from the basename or last
  URL path segment). It is required for inline `dataUrl` and `base64` payloads.
- Inline `dataUrl` / `base64` payloads are capped by the same IPC body-size limit
  as large request bodies.

**Tab behavior**

| Aspect         | Behavior                                                                      |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab label      | Shortened filename (middle ellipsis, extension preserved)                     |
| Page header    | Full filename                                                                 |
| Deduping       | Reopening the same source focuses the existing tab                            |
| Persistence    | Restored on restart until the user closes the tab                             |
| In-tab actions | **Copy location** (path, URL, or data URL) and **Download** via a save dialog |

host.openRequestDraft.title: hc.host.openRequestDraft(payload)
host.openRequestDraft.description:
Opens a new unsaved request tab seeded with request metadata. Omitted fields use
HarborClient defaults (`GET`, no body, empty headers/params). `headers` is a
flat map; `params` is an array of enabled query parameter rows.

host.send.title: hc.host.send()
host.send.description: Sends the active request editor tab using the same pipeline as the Send button. No-op when a send is already in flight for the active tab.

examples.code: await hc.host.send();

host.showEntityContextMenu.title: hc.host.showEntityContextMenu(input)
host.showEntityContextMenu.description:
Opens the same collection / folder / request context menu the built-in
Collections tree would show — including plugin
[`registerContextMenuItem`](/api/ui#hcuiregistercontextmenuitemitem)
contributions — positioned in the **host** window. Fire-and-forget; does not
wait for the user to dismiss the menu.

The host offsets `x`/`y` by the HostedSurface bounding rect. When the surface
cannot be found, coordinates are treated as host viewport coordinates.

**Limitations**

- Document targets are not supported (v1).
- Submenu flyouts and focus return to the webview may be imperfect across the
  webview boundary.
- Menu actions dispatch host thunks and work even when the built-in Collections
  tree is unmounted (replacement mode).

See the [sidebar replacement tree example](/examples/sidebar-replacement-tree)
for a full pattern including reorder/move.

params.name: x`, `y
params.description: Coordinates in the plugin webview viewport

params.name: pluginId
params.description: Your plugin manifest id (for HostedSurface lookup and focus return)

params.name: contributionId
params.description: Sidebar panel contribution id mounted in the surface

http.onAfterScripts.title: hc.http.onAfterScripts(handler)
http.onAfterScripts.description:
Register a callback that runs after each request stage's scripts complete. Fires twice per send — once after pre-request scripts and once after post-request scripts. Requires the `scripts:inject` permission.

The context includes the final `data` bag for the stage, named `hc.test` results, console lines, and script error messages. Use this to collect injected test results or correlate values scripts wrote into `hc.data`.

http.onAfterSend.title: hc.http.onAfterSend(handler)
http.onAfterSend.description:
Register a callback that runs after the response is received. Requires the `http` permission.

For UI-only plugins that react to completed sends (history, recent-requests, response diff), prefer renderer-side `hc.http.onAfterSend` in the renderer entry — it fires in-process with no main entry, custom IPC channel, or polling. Use this main-process hook when you need to run logic in the SES-hardened utilityProcess or mutate shared main-side state.

http.onBeforeScripts.title: hc.http.onBeforeScripts(handler)
http.onBeforeScripts.description:
Register a callback that runs before each request stage's scripts. Fires twice per send — once with `phase: 'pre'` and once with `phase: 'post'`. Requires the `scripts:inject` permission.

Injected scripts run as a synthetic scope ahead of collection/folder/request scripts. Within each stage (`before-all`, `before-each`, `main`, `after-each`, `after-all`), plugin scripts run before host scripts in that stage. Use `context.scripts.data` to seed the shared `hc.data` bag visible to every script in the send.

See [Baseline tests](/examples/baseline-tests), [Trace correlation](/examples/trace-correlation), and [Production guard](/examples/production-guard) for complete walkthroughs.

http.onBeforeSend.title: hc.http.onBeforeSend(handler)
http.onBeforeSend.description: Register a callback that runs before each outgoing HTTP request. Mutate the request object to change method, URL, headers, or body. Requires the `http` permission. Remove a header with `delete request.headers['Header-Name']`.

imports.registerHandler.title: hc.imports.registerHandler(extensions, handler)
imports.registerHandler.description:
| Callback    | Type                                                | Description                                         |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `canImport` | `(file: ImportFile) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Returns whether this handler should import the file |
| `import`    | `(file: ImportFile) => void \| Promise<void>`       | Performs the import workflow                        |

`ImportFile` includes `name`, `path`, `extension` (dot-prefixed, lowercase), and UTF-8 `contents`.

Extensions may be passed with or without a leading dot (`json` and `.json` are equivalent). Register multiple extensions in one call: `['.json', '.yaml', '.yml']`.

ipc.handle.title: hc.ipc.handle(channel, handler)
ipc.handle.description:
Expose an RPC channel callable from the renderer half of the same plugin. Requires the `ipc` permission.

Main-process hooks are invoked by posting work to the utilityProcess runner; the main process applies mutations and enforces permissions before and after each callback.

See the [Request logger example](/examples/request-logger) for a main-only plugin using HTTP hooks.

ipc.invoke.title: hc.ipc.invoke(channel, ...args)
ipc.invoke.description:
Invokes a handler registered with `hc.ipc.handle` in the main entry. Use `hc.pluginId` for logging — channel names are automatically scoped to your plugin.

Do not call `window.api.invokePluginMain` directly — use this typed API instead.

examples.code: const pending = await hc.ipc.invoke<Array<{ id: string }>>('pullPending');

livePage.title: hc.livePage
livePage.description:
Opens or reuses an embedded browser tab and returns a control handle (focus, close, DOM query/evaluate/inject, viewport screenshot).

Requires the `browser` permission (granted at install/enable). This is independent of Settings → General → Allow script live page access, which only gates request-script `hc.livePage`. Saving a screenshot with `page.screenshot` also requires `filesystem:write`.

Omit `url` to bind the active browser tab. Pass `{ reuse: false }` to always open a new tab (default `reuse` is `true`). New tabs wait for load before the promise resolves.

liveServers.create.title: hc.liveServers.create(input)

liveServers.delete.title: hc.liveServers.delete(id)

liveServers.get.title: hc.liveServers.get(idOrUuid)

liveServers.getLogs.title: hc.liveServers.getLogs(query)

liveServers.getStatus.title: hc.liveServers.getStatus(query)
liveServers.getStatus.signature: (query: { id: string } | { savedId: number }) => Promise<RunningLiveServer | null>
liveServers.getStatus.description: Returns the running instance for the query, or `null` when not running.

liveServers.list.title: hc.liveServers.list()
liveServers.list.description: Lists saved live servers from the local registry.

liveServers.onRequestLog.title: hc.liveServers.onRequestLog(listener)
liveServers.onRequestLog.description: Subscribes to Express access-log lines from running live servers.

liveServers.onRunningChanged.title: hc.liveServers.onRunningChanged(listener)
liveServers.onRunningChanged.description: Subscribes to start/stop list changes (including changes from the Harbor UI).

liveServers.start.title: hc.liveServers.start(input)
liveServers.start.description: Starts from `savedId` (loads config from the registry when `config` is omitted) and/or an ad-hoc `config`. Returns the running instance with assigned port and `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` origin.

liveServers.stop.title: hc.liveServers.stop(query)
liveServers.stop.description: Stops one running instance by runtime id or saved id.

liveServers.update.title: hc.liveServers.update(input)
liveServers.update.description: Updates a saved server. Does not restart a running instance.

mcp.registerServer.title: hc.mcp.registerServer(config)
mcp.registerServer.description: Discovered tools are prefixed with `mcp__` in the chat agent tool list, using the same naming scheme as user-configured MCP client servers.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Display name in Settings → AI & MCP

fields.name: serverURL
fields.description: Absolute HTTP or HTTPS MCP endpoint URL

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: When false, Harbor skips connecting. Defaults to `true

fields.name: headers
fields.description: Optional HTTP headers sent with MCP client requests

fields.description: Optional square icon as a `data:image/...;base64,...` URI for settings rows

pluginId.title: hc.pluginId
pluginId.description:
**Type:** `string`

The plugin manifest `id`. Use for IPC routing and logging instead of hardcoding the manifest id in plugin source.

react.title: hc.react
react.description:
**Type:** `typeof React`

The same React instance HarborClient uses in the renderer. Do not import or bundle `react` / `react-dom` in your plugin bundle.

scripts.title: hc.scripts
scripts.description:
Creates a script sandbox that exposes the **same `hc` object** as collection and request pre/post scripts. Use it to run tests, mutate a request snapshot, or read a response with `hc.response.json()` inside your main entry.

No extra permission is required. Contexts start with only the hc API plus globals you inject with `setVariable` and `setFunction`.

### PluginScriptContext

| Method                     | Description                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `setVariable(name, value)` | Injects a global variable visible to subsequent `run()` calls.                                                           |
| `setFunction(name, fn)`    | Injects a global function; overrides built-in globals such as `console` when names collide.                              |
| `run(script)`              | Evaluates script synchronously; returns {@link PluginScriptRunResult} with hc mutations and the last-expression `value`. |

`run()` returns the full structured result: mutated `request`, `variableSets`, `collectionVariableSets`, `environmentVariableSets`, `globalVariableSets`, `collectionHeaders`, `tests`, `logs`, `data` (the final `hc.data` bag), optional `error`, and `value` (the script's last expression).

The hc surface matches pre/post request scripts: `hc.request`, `hc.collection`, `hc.environment`, `hc.globals`, `hc.data`, `hc.test`, `hc.expect`, and `hc.response` (when `init.response` is provided). Pass optional `init.data` to seed `hc.data` when creating a context. See [Request scripts](https://harborclient.com/request-scripts) for the full hc reference, including [hc.data](https://harborclient.com/scripting#hcdata).

Tests, logs, and `hc.data` accumulate across multiple `run()` calls on the same context. Request and variable mutations persist until you create a new context.

server.onRequest.title: hc.server.onRequest(handler)
server.onRequest.description:
Invoked for each incoming HTTP request. The `request` object includes a default `echo` payload (args, data, files, form, headers, json, origin, url).

Return either:

- A JSON-serializable value for a **legacy** body-only response (always HTTP 200 + `application/json`), or
- A **structured** `PluginServerHttpResponse` with `kind: 'http-response'` (use `createHttpResponse(...)` from `@harborclient/sdk/runtime-utils`) for custom status, headers, body, and `delayMs`.

String `body` values are sent as raw text (default `text/plain` unless you set `Content-Type`). Other bodies use JSON.

Multiple handlers may be registered; each call returns a `Disposable` that removes only that handler. Handlers run sequentially in registration order. When a handler returns `undefined` or `null`, the host keeps the result from the previous handler (starting from the default echo payload).

server.start.title: hc.server.start(options?)
server.start.description: Starts listening. Returns the assigned port after the server accepts connections.

server.stop.title: hc.server.stop()
server.stop.description: Stops the echo server owned by this plugin.

storage.get.title: hc.storage.get(key)
storage.get.description: Returns the stored value, or `undefined` if the key has never been set.

storage.set.title: hc.storage.set(key, value)
storage.set.description:
Persists a JSON-serializable value.

Invalid JSON already stored for a key causes `get` to throw with a plugin-scoped error message (same behavior as the renderer API).

examples.code:
await hc.storage.set('accessToken', refreshedToken);
await hc.storage.set('links', [{ collectionId: 1, dotenvPath: '/path/to/.env' }]);

themes.getActive.title: hc.themes.getActive()
themes.getActive.description: Returns the currently active theme — either a built-in id or a plugin theme reference.

themes.onDidChange.title: hc.themes.onDidChange(listener)
themes.onDidChange.description: Fires when the user changes the appearance theme in Settings or when the host resets theme after plugin deactivation.

themes.register.title: hc.themes.register(theme)
themes.register.description:
Provide `colors`, `metrics`, a `stylesheet`, or a combination. Use `colors` / `metrics` for token swaps; use `stylesheet` when you need selectors beyond `:root` (for example plugin-specific tweaks under `[data-theme='plugin-…']`).

When the user selects your theme, the persisted value is `plugin:<pluginId>:<themeId>`. If the plugin is disabled or uninstalled while its theme is active, HarborClient falls back to **System**.

fields.description: Theme id unique within your plugin

fields.name: type
fields.description: Sets `color-scheme` and Electron native chrome base

fields.name: metrics
fields.description: Optional typography/geometry overrides (CSS strings such as `14px`)

fields.name: stylesheet
fields.description: Optional plugin-relative CSS file for complex themes

ui.closeModal.title: hc.ui.closeModal(modalId?)
ui.closeModal.description: Closes the open plugin modal overlay. When `modalId` is provided, the overlay closes only if that modal is currently open.

ui.openModal.title: hc.ui.openModal(modalId, context?)
ui.openModal.description: Opens the registered modal overlay in the host application window. Optional `context` is passed to the modal component as a `context` prop.

ui.registerCollectionSettingsTab.title: hc.ui.registerCollectionSettingsTab(tab)
ui.registerCollectionSettingsTab.description: Adds a segmented tab to Collection Settings (alongside General, Variables, Headers, and so on). The component receives `context.collectionId` and `context.readOnly`.

fields.name: order
fields.description: Sort order among collection settings tabs

ui.registerContextMenuItem.title: hc.ui.registerContextMenuItem(item)
ui.registerContextMenuItem.description:
Adds an action to row context menus in the sidebar for **collection**,
**folder**, and **request** targets.

When a plugin replaces the Collections sidebar (`replaces: "collections"`),
those contributions still appear in menus opened via
[`hc.host.showEntityContextMenu`](/api/host#hchostshowentitycontextmenuinput)
— the host builds the same menu model the built-in tree uses. They do **not**
appear automatically inside a plugin’s own custom `RowActionsMenu` unless the
plugin calls `showEntityContextMenu` (or builds an equivalent menu and invokes
the same host commands).

Document targets are not supported. See [Host](/api/host) for
coordinate mapping and focus-return limitations.

fields.name: command
fields.description: Command id; handler receives target context as args

ui.registerFooterPanel.title: hc.ui.registerFooterPanel(panel)
ui.registerFooterPanel.description:
Registers a slide-up footer panel using the same pattern as Console and Variables.
The host wraps your component in a resizable shell — you do not implement resize
logic yourself. The shell provides:

- A top drag handle (and keyboard resize on the handle)
- Per-panel height persistence in `localStorage` (`hc.footerPanel.<namespaced-id>`)
- A close button in the top-right corner

**Layout contract:** Your `Component` should fill the resizable area with
`flex h-full min-h-0 flex-col` and put scrollable content in a
`flex-1 overflow-auto` child. Leave roughly 32px of right padding on header
rows so controls do not sit under the host close button.

To show a status dot beside the footer toggle (running / stopped / error), use
[`hc.ui.setFooterPanelIndicator`](#hcuisetfooterpanelindicatorpanelid-state) —
do not mount your own indicator UI.

Example panel structure:

fields.name: title
fields.description: Toggle label in the footer bar

ui.registerLivePageChromeAction.title: hc.ui.registerLivePageChromeAction(action)
ui.registerLivePageChromeAction.description:
Adds a RoundButton to the embedded browser chrome bar between Downloads and Ask AI. Buttons sort by **plugin activation order**, then registration order within that plugin — there is no `order` field.

The command handler receives a single {@link LivePageChromeActionContext} argument with `tabId`, `url`, `title`, and optional `websiteId`.

fields.name: command
fields.description: Command id to run on click

fields.name: icon
fields.description: Optional curated icon name (host resolves; puzzle fallback)

ui.registerMainView.title: hc.ui.registerMainView(view)
ui.registerMainView.description: Registers a full main-area overlay, replacing the request editor while open (same pattern as Team Hubs or Sharing Keys). Open the view with `hc.commands.execute` from a menu item or other trigger. The `title` and optional `icon` appear on the page tab.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Display name for the page tab

fields.name: icon
fields.description: Tab-bar icon name. Supported: `server`, `database`, `globe`, `code`, `robot`, `puzzle-piece`, `bolt`, `flask`. Unknown names fall back to `puzzle-piece`.

ui.registerMenuItem.title: hc.ui.registerMenuItem(item)
ui.registerMenuItem.description:
Adds an item to the application menu. Register the command handler with `hc.commands.register` separately.

For **File → Import** workflows, prefer [`hc.imports.registerHandler`](/api/imports) instead of adding a separate File menu import item. Built-in HarborClient formats are detected first; plugin handlers receive only unrecognized files whose extensions they registered.

fields.name: command
fields.description: Command id to run on click

ui.registerModal.title: hc.ui.registerModal(modal)
ui.registerModal.description: Registers a modal rendered in a full-window overlay at the application root. Open it with `hc.ui.openModal(modalId, context?)` and close it with `hc.ui.closeModal(modalId?)`. Requires the `ui` permission.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Accessible title for the modal surface

ui.registerRequestTab.title: hc.ui.registerRequestTab(tab)
ui.registerRequestTab.description: Adds a segmented tab to the request editor (alongside Params, Headers, Body, and so on). The component receives `context.draft` for the active request, `context.response` when a response exists, and `context.variables` for merged global, collection, and environment substitution values (see [Global variables](/api/commands)).

ui.registerRequestToolbarAction.title: hc.ui.registerRequestToolbarAction(action)
ui.registerRequestToolbarAction.description: Adds a button to the request URL bar toolbar.

fields.name: command
fields.description: Command id to run on click

fields.name: order
fields.description: Sort order near the Send button

ui.registerResponseTab.title: hc.ui.registerResponseTab(tab)
ui.registerResponseTab.description: Adds a tab to the response viewer (alongside Body, Headers, Tests).

fields.name: when
fields.description: When the tab is visible. Default `hasResponse`.

ui.registerScriptEditorAction.title: hc.ui.registerScriptEditorAction(action)
ui.registerScriptEditorAction.description:
HarborClient uses **request stage** for the pre-request and post-request script lists (`ScriptPhase`: `pre` | `post`) and **script stage** for timing within a list (`ScriptStage`: `before-all`, `before-each`, `main`, `after-each`, `after-all`).

Script rows carry a {@link ScriptStage} value that controls when the script runs within its request stage. Plugin script editor actions are not filtered by script stage today — use `phases` only.

Adds an icon button to each script row in the pre-request and post-request stage editors. The command handler receives a single {@link ScriptEditorActionContext} argument with `phase` (request stage), `scriptId`, and `code`.

fields.name: command
fields.description: Command id to run on click

fields.name: order
fields.description: Sort order within the row action group

fields.name: phases
fields.description: Optional filter — show only in pre-request and/or post-request stage tabs

ui.registerSettingsSection.title: hc.ui.registerSettingsSection(section)
ui.registerSettingsSection.description: Registers a React component as a Settings panel alongside built-in sections (General, Storage, and so on).

ui.registerSidebarPanel.title: hc.ui.registerSidebarPanel(panel)
ui.registerSidebarPanel.description:
Registers a switchable left sidebar destination — a full-height panel the user selects instead of the default collections view. The host mounts the panel with `resizeMode="fill"` so the plugin surface fills the sidebar body and scrolls inside the webview (`plugin-surface-fill`). Panel bodies should scroll via `Scrollbars` from `@harborclient/sdk/components` (OverlayScrollbars is bundled with the SDK; theme CSS comes from the host stylesheet) so they match the built-in Collections sidebar — do not use native `overflow-y-auto` for the main list.

**Replacing Collections:** To make this panel the default left-sidebar body (hiding the built-in Collections tree and "Collections" switcher tab), set `replaces: "collections"` on the matching **manifest** entry. That field is not part of the runtime `SidebarPanelContribution` object; the host copies it from the manifest at registration time.

Semantics:

- `activeSidebarPanelId === null` means the **primary collections surface** — the replacement panel when one is registered, otherwise the built-in Collections tree.
- Non-replacing plugin panels remain switchable destinations alongside the primary surface.
- When multiple panels claim `replaces: "collections"`, the host picks one winner (lowest `order`, then `pluginId`, then contribution `id`) and logs a warning.

For activity-rail icons that open a sidebar while keeping the rail visible, use
[hc.ui.registerSidebarRailItem](#hcuiregistersidebarrailitemitem) instead.

ui.registerSidebarRailItem.title: hc.ui.registerSidebarRailItem(item)
ui.registerSidebarRailItem.description:
Registers an activity-rail button. Selecting it mounts the panel with `resizeMode="fill"` and **keeps the activity rail visible** (unlike `registerSidebarPanel`, which uses a horizontal switcher and hides the rail). Panel bodies should scroll via `Scrollbars` from `@harborclient/sdk/components`.

The host pushes `{ sidebarSelection }` as surface context (same shape as sidebar panels). Prefer `hc.host.onSidebarSelectionChanged` for live updates.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Label / accessible name on the activity rail

fields.name: order
fields.description: Sort order among plugin rail items (appended after built-in modes)

ui.registerSidebarSection.title: hc.ui.registerSidebarSection(section)
ui.registerSidebarSection.description: Adds a collapsible block inside the scrollable sidebar, using the same pattern as the built-in Collections and Environments sections.

fields.name: headerActions
fields.description: Optional controls in the section header row

ui.registerStatusBarItem.title: hc.ui.registerStatusBarItem(item)
ui.registerStatusBarItem.description: Adds a custom status indicator to the footer bar.

ui.registerWorkflowActionBlock.title: hc.ui.registerWorkflowActionBlock(block)
ui.registerWorkflowActionBlock.description:
Renders a HostedSurface inside matching workflow timeline action blocks (below
the built-in thumbnail). Surfaces are skipped when the block is compact (too
narrow). Prefer a narrow `actionTypes` list to avoid mounting many webviews.

fields.name: actionTypes
fields.description: Optional filter — omit to show on every timeline action

fields.name: order
fields.description: Sort order among stacked surfaces in a block

ui.registerWorkflowToolbarAction.title: hc.ui.registerWorkflowToolbarAction(action)
ui.registerWorkflowToolbarAction.description:
Adds a button to the right of Save in the workflow play/edit toolbar. The
command handler receives a single `WorkflowToolbarActionContext` argument with
`workflowId`, `actionIndex`, `action`, and `dirty`.

fields.name: command
fields.description: Command id to run on click

fields.name: order
fields.description: Sort order to the right of Save

ui.setFooterPanelIndicator.title: hc.ui.setFooterPanelIndicator(panelId, state)
ui.setFooterPanelIndicator.description:
Sets or clears the native status dot beside a footer panel toggle. The host
renders a `StatusDot`; plugins do not mount an indicator webview.

`FooterPanelIndicatorState`:

| Field    | Type                                                                  | Description                          |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `status` | `'success' \| 'danger' \| 'muted' \| 'accent' \| 'warning' \| 'info'` | Color preset for the status dot      |
| `label`  | `string`                                                              | Optional accessible name for the dot |

Call from the agent (always-on) renderer after registering the panel, and again
whenever status changes:

params.name: state
params.description: Indicator status, or `null` to hide the dot

ui.showToast.title: hc.ui.showToast(message, options?)
ui.showToast.description: Shows a non-blocking toast for success or info feedback. Do not use toasts for errors that require acknowledgment — show those inline in your plugin UI instead.

examples.code: hc.ui.showToast('Settings saved', { duration: 3000 });
